name: Diazoxide-resistant focal hyperinsulinism due to Kir6.2 deficiency
aliases: Focal congenital hyperinsulinism with Kir6.2 mutation

criteria.description: Persistent hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin levels
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the KCNJ11 gene encoding Kir6.2
Lack of clinical response to diazoxide therapy
Localization of focal pancreatic lesion by 18F-DOPA PET scan

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent hypoglycemia with elevated insulin, confirmed KCNJ11 mutation, and diazoxide unresponsiveness
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to differentiate focal from diffuse forms and guide surgical management.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inappropriately elevated serum insulin during hypoglycemia

searchTerms: newborn seizures caused by low blood sugar
seizures in infants due to low glucose
larger than normal baby size at birth
low blood sugar triggered by not eating

occasional.symptomName: Developmental delay secondary to recurrent hypoglycemia
searchTerms: developmental delays from low blood sugar
growth and learning problems due to hypoglycemia
low sugar with high insulin and low ketones

occasional.symptomName: Irritability and sweating during hypoglycemic episodes
searchTerms: sweating when blood sugar is low
symptoms of hypoglycemia like sweating and fussiness

occasional.notes: May be observed in some cases

rare.symptomName: Pancreatic focal lesion detected on imaging

laboratory: Hypoglycemia with elevated insulin and C-peptide levels
Normal or low free fatty acids during hypoglycemia
imaging: 18F-DOPA PET scan showing focal pancreatic lesion
Pancreatic MRI or CT may be used adjunctively
other: Lack of response to diazoxide therapy
Histopathology confirming focal adenomatous hyperplasia after surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse pancreatic involvement rather than focal lesion
Different clinical course and imaging findings

redFlags: Recurrent severe hypoglycemia unresponsive to diazoxide
Neonatal seizures or coma due to hypoglycemia
Failure to thrive or developmental delay secondary to hypoglycemia
references: De León DD, Stanley CA. Congenital Hyperinsulinism: Diagnosis and Treatment. Endocrinol Metab Clin North Am. 2018.
Snider KE, Becker S, Boyajian L, et al. Genotype and phenotype correlations in congenital hyperinsulinism due to KATP channel mutations. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2013.
